chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man buys a female slave who is pregnant; what is permissible for him from her?' He said: 'That which is below the private part.' I said: 'He buys a young girl who has not yet had her first menstruation and is not a virgin; should he purify her (istibra')?' He said: 'Her case is severe; if one like her is pregnant, he should purify her.'

key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئُهَا: To purify/verify (specifically istibra' to confirm pregnancy or end of pregnancy)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sexual relations with a newly purchased pregnant female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling of *jam' al-shawk* (preventing ejaculation) for a purchased pregnant slave girl, permitting non-vaginal intimacy while prohibiting vaginal intercourse to avoid mixing lineages. For a young, non-menstruating girl, the Imam emphasizes the severity of the situation due to the uncertainty of her pregnancy status, advising *istibra'* (purification through a period of waiting or sexual abstinence) to ensure clarity before consummation. This ruling highlights the practical application of lineage preservation (*nasab*) in early Shia jurisprudence regarding concubinage.
